learning.title: The CSS rail reads comments as text, so an issue number written as `#233` in a stylesheet is a raw hex colour
learning.trigger: `pnpm test:rails` fails in "shared CSS rail rejects raw visual values" with a defect like `raw color: #233`, on a stylesheet that has no colour in it, and the file only changed by gaining or editing a comment.
learning.mistake: Wrote a comment naming the issue in the usual GitHub form (`issue #233`) inside packages/ui/src/navigation.css, and read the resulting "raw color" defect as a false positive in the rail rather than as the rail doing exactly what it says: it scans the stylesheet as text, so a `#` followed by hex digits is a colour wherever it sits.
learning.rule: Keep issue references in CSS comments without the hash (`issue 233`), or leave the number out. The same rule applies to any text in a stylesheet that could read as a value: a hex-looking word after `#`, a bare `0` where a length is expected, or a number with no unit in a length position. Two more values trip the same rail and are lint-clean everywhere else: `font-weight: 600` must be `font-weight: var(--weight-semibold)`, and an outline must use `var(--focus-width)` with `var(--color-focus)`, not a literal `2px` or an invented `--color-focus-ring`. Run the rail before concluding a CSS change is green; it is a text scan, not a CSS parser.

verification.requirement: The "shared CSS rail rejects raw visual values" case passes with no defects listed for the edited stylesheet. If it reports a defect at a column that looks like a comment, read that line as text rather than as a declaration before changing anything else.
